business: TODO, a body-worn camera with a caregiver app: live video from the wearer, two-way voice, SOS and GPS
target: US family caregivers of a vulnerable person: parents of a child with autism or an intellectual disability who may wander, and adult children caring for a parent with dementia

segments.name: Parent of a child with autism or intellectual disability (wanders or is non-verbal)
Adult child caring for a parent with dementia, living nearby or long-distance
Spouse or relative of an adult with a disability who wants independence with a safety net

behaviours.name: Already uses a tracker
behaviours.how: Pays monthly for AngelSense, a medical alert pendant or a kids' watch today and compares everything to it.

behaviours.name: Researches for weeks
behaviours.how: Reads Facebook support groups, Reddit and reviews before buying anything for their loved one.

behaviours.name: Crisis buyer
behaviours.how: Recently had a scare (a wandering incident, a fall, police called) and wants something now.

behaviours.name: Tight budget
behaviours.how: Already pays for therapy, care or medication; every monthly fee is weighed hard.

behaviours.name: Privacy-minded
behaviours.how: Worries about dignity and consent, and does not want their loved one to feel watched.

behaviours.name: Low-tech
behaviours.how: Wants something that works out of the box; gives up if setup takes more than a few minutes.

objections: They will just pull it off or refuse to wear it
Battery life: I already charge AngelSense every night and live video will be worse
Another monthly fee on top of everything else
A camera on my loved one feels like surveillance; what about their dignity and other people's privacy?
Is this a new brand I can trust when it really matters?
An AirTag or a kids' watch does most of this for much less
Will the video actually connect in a real emergency?
habits: you are in a Facebook group for parents of autistic kids
your child once got out of the house and police found them two streets away
you live two hours from your mother, who has early-stage Alzheimer's
you check a location app several times a day
your father refuses anything that looks like a medical device
you work full time and coordinate care by phone
